project: Conan — v4.1: Tauri terminal-wrapper for Claude Code (beefed-up TUI)
description: v4.1 pivots Conan from a sprawling web dashboard to a terminal-primary native desktop app: the Claude Code terminal as the main surface, with a DevTools-style widget HUD (exactly two widgets to start — Context (session) + Usage (global) — plus the Pulse graph), shipped via Tauri v2 with the existing Node gateway running as a Tauri sidecar. Stories are dependency-ordered: first STRIP the v2/v3 IA (sidebar nav + route views, then the timeline-primary Overview) keeping the build green at each step, then RESHAPE to terminal-primary + the HUD, then add the Tauri shell and package the gateway sidecar. Source: docs/v4.1-backlog.md + prd-claude-code-dashboard.md (## v4.1). Tauri/native-module packaging research (the dominant risk): docs/v4.1-research.md. The preview/build feature was already removed in QA before this loop.

userStories.title: Scaffold Tauri v2 at the repo root, wired to the existing Vite UI
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a Tauri v2 project at the repo root so Conan can run as a native desktop window reusing the existing React + xterm UI.
acceptanceCriteria: Add @tauri-apps/cli (dev dep) + @tauri-apps/api and @tauri-apps/plugin-shell; create src-tauri/ at the repo root (NOT inside ui/) via tauri init

tauri.conf.json (v2 schema) wires build.beforeDevCommand='npm --prefix ui run dev', beforeBuildCommand='npm --prefix ui run build', devUrl='http://localhost:5173', frontendDist='../ui/dist'; productName 'Conan', identifier 'so.whatmatters.conan'; a single 1400x900 window; bundle.targets ['app','dmg']
Set Vite to a fixed port (5173) and clearScreen:false so Tauri can attach to the dev server

Add npm scripts (e.g. tauri:dev, tauri:build) and document Rust/Tauri prerequisites in docs/ (rustup + tauri-cli); if the Rust toolchain is unavailable on the build host, install it via rustup or clearly note the gap in progress.txt
cargo check (or tauri info) succeeds for the scaffolded src-tauri crate; the gateway still builds
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build is clean
userStories.notes: Anchors + exact config in docs/v4.1-research.md §1. The sidecar (US-008/009) and origin/CSP (US-007) come later; this story is just scaffolding. Keep .gitignore'ing src-tauri/target. No browser-verify (native shell).

userStories.title: Rewire the UI to an absolute gateway base under Tauri (keep same-origin in browser dev)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the webview to reach the gateway at an absolute loopback URL when running under Tauri, since the Tauri webview origin (tauri://localhost) differs from the gateway origin, while browser dev keeps using the Vite proxy.
acceptanceCriteria: Introduce a single gateway-base resolver (e.g. ui/src/lib/gateway.ts) that returns 'http://127.0.0.1:3747' when running under Tauri (detect via '__TAURI_INTERNALS__' in window) and '' (same-origin, Vite-proxied) otherwise

Route the same-origin fetches and WebSocket URLs through the resolver: /api/config + /api/health in App.tsx, the app WS (useGateway/useTasks), the terminal WS (Terminal.tsx), and any remaining /api/* fetches in the surviving hooks (useSessions, useUsage, useWidgets, usePulse, useTerminals)
Browser behavior is unchanged (relative URLs still hit the Vite proxy at :5173 and same-origin at :3747); no regression to the web-served app
WS URLs build ws://127.0.0.1:3747/... under Tauri and same-origin ws otherwise, preserving the ?token= param
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build is clean
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill that the web-served app at :3747 still connects (config loads, WS connected, terminal opens) with the resolver in place
userStories.notes: docs/v4.1-research.md §4. The token still comes from /api/config; cross-origin fetch to 127.0.0.1:3747 works in the Tauri webview. Pinning CONAN_PORT=3747 (US-009 sidecar env) keeps the hard-coded base safe.

userStories.title: Gateway Origin allowlist + CSP accept the Tauri webview origin

acceptanceCriteria: Extend allowedOrigins() in src/gateway/auth.ts (defaults ~:43-61) to include tauri://localhost (plus http://tauri.localhost and https://tauri.localhost for cross-platform/future-proofing), OR ensure CONAN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS carries them — keep http://localhost:5173 and the :3747 loopback defaults intact
verifyUpgradeOrigin accepts the Tauri origin on /ws and /ws/terminal upgrades and still rejects unknown origins (CVE-2025-52882 floor unchanged)

Document/define the Tauri CSP option in docs/v4.1-research.md/backlog (connect-src for http+ws loopback) and set app.security.csp in tauri.conf.json (null is acceptable for a loopback desktop app, or the explicit connect-src policy)
Add a small test (scripts/test-*.mjs) or extend an existing auth test asserting a tauri://localhost Origin is allowed and a bogus origin is rejected
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build is clean
userStories.notes: Edits src/gateway/auth.ts — run the loop agent outside the in-dock session (footgun #1). docs/v4.1-research.md §4. No browser-verify needed; cover via the auth unit test.

userStories.title: Package the Node gateway as a sidecar binary (prove node-pty + better-sqlite3 work)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the gateway built into a self-contained sidecar artifact named with the target triple, with its native addons working, since this is the dominant packaging risk.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a reproducible build script (e.g. scripts/build-sidecar.mjs + an npm script) that produces src-tauri/binaries/conan-gateway-<TARGET_TRIPLE> (e.g. conan-gateway-aarch64-apple-darwin); approach = bundled-node launcher (ship node + a node_modules with arm64 prebuilds) OR @yao-pkg/pkg carrying the addons as assets (see docs/v4.1-research.md §3)
node-pty's spawn-helper travels AND retains its executable (+x) bit in the packaged artifact (the posix_spawnp footgun) — chmod at build/runtime if the packager drops it

Running the produced binary directly (no Tauri) on this machine: it serves GET /api/health with 200 and a terminal WS can spawn a pty (exercise the two native addons — better-sqlite3 DB open + node-pty spawn)
The binary is ad-hoc codesigned (codesign -s -) so the arm64 kernel doesn't kill it; document the distribution-signing requirement
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build is clean
userStories.notes: THE HARD PART — docs/v4.1-research.md §3 (native-module gotchas). Match the Node ABI used to package to the prebuilt .node files. Validate the two failure-prone things explicitly: open the DB, open a pty. No browser-verify (binary-level).

userStories.title: Spawn the gateway sidecar from Tauri (start on launch, kill on exit) + capability
userStories.description: As a user, I want launching the Conan desktop app to start the bundled gateway and the terminal + widgets to work end-to-end, with the gateway cleanly killed on quit.
acceptanceCriteria: Register tauri-plugin-shell and grant the shell:allow-spawn capability for the conan-gateway sidecar in src-tauri/capabilities/default.json

In src-tauri/src/lib.rs: spawn the sidecar in the setup hook with env CONAN_PORT=3747 and CONAN_ALLOWED_ORIGINS including tauri://localhost; hold the CommandChild in Tauri state and kill it on RunEvent::ExitRequested (a leaked sidecar blocks the single-instance :3747 on next launch)
Pipe sidecar stdout/stderr to the Tauri log for debugging

cargo check passes; tauri dev launches the window, the webview reaches the sidecar gateway (config loads, app WS connected), and a terminal opens with a live pty; quitting the app terminates the sidecar (port :3747 is free afterward)
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build is clean
userStories.notes: docs/v4.1-research.md §2. Depends on US-006 (absolute base), US-007 (origin), US-008 (the binary). If the Rust/Tauri toolchain can't run a full launch on the build host, verify cargo check + the wiring and note the manual E2E step in progress.txt. No browser-verify (native).
